diagnoses.headline: AJ200D Timing Chain Tensioner Wear
diagnoses.summary: Cold-start rattle on pre-2019 Ingenium diesels that can progress from tensioner wear to chain failure and serious engine damage if ignored.

overrideCopy.headline: Do not keep driving on a cold-start chain rattle
overrideCopy.body: If the Ingenium chain slips, the car can move from a tensioner repair into full engine replacement territory in one event.
actions: Avoid repeated cold restarts if the rattle is already severe.
Arrange recovery rather than driving long distances.
Confirm chain stretch and tensioner condition before pricing the rest of the car.

nextSteps: Confirm cold-start rattle from the timing-chain area, not accessory drive noise.
Have a Jaguar specialist inspect tensioner and chain stretch before authorising replacement.
Compare car value against the reconditioned engine range before committing.

diagnoses.headline: AJ133 5.0 V8 Chain Tensioner (pre-2013)
diagnoses.summary: Documented timing-chain tensioner risk on early AJ133 5.0 V8 engines. The 2013 revision largely resolved it, but pre-2013 cars still need a careful check.

overrideCopy.headline: Treat early AJ133 chain noise as urgent
overrideCopy.body: Pre-2013 AJ133 tensioner failure can escalate quickly from a warning rattle into catastrophic valvetrain damage.
actions: Stop long-distance driving if chain noise is present.
Verify whether the engine is a pre-2013 build or revised unit.
Budget for specialist inspection before any major ownership decision.

nextSteps: Confirm build date and whether the tensioner revision was completed.
Get a Jaguar specialist to inspect chain condition and oil history.
Use XJ/XF retained values against the upper recon range before walking away.

diagnoses.headline: 276DT (2.7 TDV6) Oil Pump Failure
diagnoses.summary: Shared with Land Rover Discovery 3 — oil pump failure often kills the engine outright with little warning. One of the most expensive Jaguar failure paths in our data.

overrideCopy.headline: Oil-pressure loss on a 276DT is an emergency
overrideCopy.body: This failure mode often ends as a dead engine. Continuing to drive after low oil pressure or sudden cut-out risks a total write-off of the unit.
actions: Stop driving immediately if oil pressure warning or sudden power loss appears.
Recover the car — do not restart repeatedly.
Confirm whether repair is still possible before pricing a replacement engine.

nextSteps: Capture fault codes and oil-pressure history if the engine still runs.
Get a specialist strip assessment before committing to recon.
Compare vehicle value carefully — many 276DT cars sit close to replacement cost.

diagnoses.headline: AJ126 Cooling System / Chain Tensioner
diagnoses.summary: AJ126 V6 cars can combine cooling-system weakness with chain-tensioner concerns. Heat and timing noise together should be treated as an urgent ownership decision.

overrideCopy.headline: Do not ignore overheating plus timing noise
overrideCopy.body: On AJ126, cooling faults and chain concerns can stack into a much larger bill if secondary damage starts.
actions: Park up if temperature climbs or coolant loss is visible.
Check for chain noise on cold start before authorising limited repairs.
Ask for a full cooling + timing inspection, not a single-part guess.

nextSteps: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect for external leaks.
Confirm chain condition before quoting repair alone.
Compare recon vs rebuild once the full fault set is known.

diagnoses.headline: Ingenium Petrol Water Pump (AJ200P / 204PT)
diagnoses.summary: The Ingenium petrol is one of the cleaner Jaguar engines in our data — water pump replacement is the main meaningful weak point rather than a catastrophic failure pattern.
diagnoses.evidenceLabel: EM-VERIFIED common Ingenium petrol service path

overrideCopy.headline: Monitor coolant loss early
overrideCopy.body: This path is usually repairable if caught before overheating damage spreads into the rest of the engine.
actions: Check coolant level regularly once seepage starts.
Avoid long trips with a low coolant warning.
Replace the pump before secondary heat damage appears.

nextSteps: Confirm whether the leak is pump, housing, or hose related.
Repair is usually proportionate — replacement is rarely the first answer.
Keep service history notes; this engine otherwise has a strong record in our data.

diagnoses.headline: Turbocharger Wear / Failure
diagnoses.summary: Whistle, smoke under load, or limp mode on turbocharged Jaguar engines often points to turbo wear, actuator faults, or related oil feed issues.

overrideCopy.headline: Limp mode plus smoke needs a stop-and-check
overrideCopy.body: Continuing to drive a failing turbo can push metal debris through the engine and turn a turbo job into a full replacement.
actions: Reduce load and avoid boost if smoke or whistle worsens.
Check oil level and recent service history.
Inspect for shaft play and oil feed restriction before quoting.

nextSteps: Confirm turbo vs intake/boost-leak symptoms with a specialist.
Budget actuator or turbo assembly repair first where possible.
Only escalate to engine replacement if secondary damage is confirmed.

diagnoses.headline: Oil Leaks & Consumption
diagnoses.summary: Rising oil use, blue smoke, or external leaks are common ownership complaints. Severity depends on whether the issue is a gasket leak or internal consumption.

overrideCopy.headline: Track oil use before it becomes an engine decision
overrideCopy.body: External leaks are often contained. Rapid internal consumption needs diagnosis before you assume a full engine is required.
actions: Log oil top-ups over a fixed mileage window.
Inspect for external leaks before authorising major work.
Smoke on overrun points more toward internal sealing issues.

nextSteps: Separate external leak from true burning/consumption.
Repair gaskets or breathers first where evidence supports it.
Reassess against car value only if consumption stays severe after basic fixes.

diagnoses.headline: Exhaust / Emissions System Faults
diagnoses.summary: DPF, EGR, and emissions warnings are frequent on Jaguar diesels. Many stay repairable, but ignored clogging can cascade into turbo and engine damage.

overrideCopy.headline: Do not ignore repeated DPF or EGR warnings
overrideCopy.body: Emissions faults left unresolved often become boost, overheating, or oil-contamination problems.
actions: Avoid repeated aborted regenerations on short trips.
Scan for EGR/DPF codes before replacing random sensors.
Check for oil or coolant contamination if the fault keeps returning.

nextSteps: Get a proper diagnostics session, not a parts-cannon approach.
Confirm whether cleaning, sensor repair, or EGR replacement is the real fix.
Escalate only if contamination or turbo damage is already present.

diagnoses.headline: Battery / Electrical Issues
diagnoses.summary: Flat batteries, warning clusters, and start-stop faults are common and usually far cheaper than engine work — but they can mask charging or module problems.

overrideCopy.headline: Rule out the simple electrical faults first
overrideCopy.body: Most electrical complaints do not justify engine replacement maths. Diagnose battery and charging health before escalating.
actions: Test battery and charging system under load.
Check for parasitic drain if the car goes flat overnight.
Confirm software/module warnings after a quality battery fit.

nextSteps: Start with battery health and IBS coding where required.
Only investigate deeper modules after a healthy charge system is confirmed.
Keep this path separate from true mechanical engine failures.

diagnoses.headline: Spark / Ignition Faults
diagnoses.summary: Misfires, rough idle, and coil or plug failures are common on petrol Jaguars and usually land in repair territory rather than replacement.

overrideCopy.headline: Misfire is usually a repair-first problem
overrideCopy.body: Unless the misfire has already caused catalyst or internal damage, coils and plugs are the proportionate first move.
actions: Do not keep driving in severe misfire for long distances.
Scan for cylinder-specific codes before replacing parts at random.
Inspect for oil in plug wells if covers are leaking.

nextSteps: Replace plugs/coils on the affected bank or as a set where recommended.
Recheck for misfire after repair before considering deeper engine work.
Only escalate if compression or catalyst damage is confirmed.
